claims.text: Grants support the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers.
Grants support research that expands the appreciation of sculpture.
The categories for grants are New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications, Long-Term Research, and Research and Travel.
Applications are considered four times per year.
Applications are submitted via Flexi-Grant.
New Projects and Commissions grants are for exhibitions, exhibition catalogues, and sculpture commissions.
The maximum grant available for New Projects and Commissions is £20,000.
Acquisitions and Collections grants are for acquiring new sculptural works for collections, or to conserve sculpture in existing collections, and can also cover cataloguing and display costs.
The maximum grant available for Acquisitions and Collections is £20,000.
Conferences, Lectures and Publications grants are for publishing a new book or journal, or staging a conference or other event related to sculpture.
The maximum grant awarded for Conferences, Lectures and Publications is £5,000.
Long-Term Research grants support extended research projects requiring funding for more than one year.
The maximum grant available for Long-Term Research is £20,000.
Research and Travel grants are available to sculpture historians, academics and conservators.
Research and Travel grants support research costs, travel, photography and archival access for those researching and publishing on sculpture conservation, production, history and/or interpretation.
The maximum grant available for Research and Travel is £2,500.
Applications are considered four times per year, with specific submission deadlines for Autumn, Winter, Spring, and Summer rounds.
Organisations must be registered to apply for a grant.
Registration requests must be received one week before the deadline.
